buttonLabel: "Explore nature in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru"
lead: >-
  Bolivia's flamingo lagoons and the Galápagos Islands with their giant tortoises offer two very different encounters with nature. Peru adds the high-altitude landscapes of Titicaca, while Colombia provides the surroundings of Guatapé. We explain which wildlife encounters genuinely form part of the itinerary, which island excursions are alternatives and why the four-country filter refers to a longer journey.
---

## Where to watch wildlife on a journey through Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru

This thematic selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: ["8 South American Countries in 32 Days"](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). The countries in the title are **part of a longer itinerary** that also passes through Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Chile. This is crucial for planning: you cannot combine the four selected countries in any order and obtain the same program.

The main wildlife-watching stops are in Bolivia and Ecuador. The Peruvian section centers on Titicaca and Inca monuments, while Colombia features cities and the landscapes around Guatapé. The itinerary does not promise a separate safari in Peru or Colombia. The "Wildlife and Safaris" interest here is grounded in the fauna of Bolivia's lagoons and the Galápagos; salt flats, mountain lakes and Guatapé's scenery also belong to the separate ["Nature"](/interests/nature/) interest.

## Bolivia: high-altitude lagoon birds, not jungle

After Chile, the itinerary enters Bolivia's Altiplano: travelers in 4×4 vehicles pass Laguna Verde, the Sol de Mañana geysers and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), where flamingos live. The route then continues past other lagoons to [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/).

The birds, mineral lakes and stark high-altitude scenery are all appealing here. It is impossible to guarantee flamingos at a specific location or distance in advance. Bring warm clothing and protection against wind and sun; the principal physical demands are **altitude and long road transfers**. The current itinerary includes an acclimatization stop in San Pedro de Atacama before the Bolivian days.

## Ecuador: Santa Cruz tortoises and one of two island routes

On [the Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), the nature program is different. Upon reaching Santa Cruz, travelers take [an excursion into the highlands to see giant tortoises and lava tunnels](/ecuador/santa-cruz-highlands/santa-cruz-highlands-lava-tunnels/). This land-based stage allows visitors to encounter animals in their natural habitat.

The following day follows **one of two alternatives**, confirmed after booking:

- [North Seymour and Bachas Beaches](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/north-seymour-island-tour/): a boat excursion and opportunities to see frigatebirds and blue-footed boobies;
- [South Plaza and Cape Carrión](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/south-plaza-island-tour/): an island excursion where characteristic animals include sea lions and land iguanas.

Both excursions are not included simultaneously in the price of the 32-day journey. In protected areas, keep your distance from animals, never feed them and remain on permitted paths. A telephoto lens is useful for photography; an encounter with a particular animal at close range is not guaranteed.

## Peru and Colombia: what they add to the nature experience

After the overland crossing from Bolivia, the Peruvian leg includes [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), then [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). This is a striking transition from Andean scenery to history and archaeology. The Peruvian stage has no separate wildlife-watching tour.

Colombia begins in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). A trip to [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) reveals the reservoir and green hills; next come [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/). These are primarily scenic and cultural stops, rather than excursions to find rare animals.

## Planning nature days without losing the itinerary

Bolivia and the Galápagos present opposite demands. On the Altiplano, travelers must be ready for altitude and road journeys; on the islands, for boat trips and the rules of protected nature areas. Peru and a flight to Ecuador lie between them on the actual itinerary, so these two nature stages cannot be treated as neighboring day trips.

If giant tortoises, seabirds and iguanas are your main goal, look at [multi-country "Wildlife and Safaris" tours](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/) and the actual Galápagos section. If mountain lagoons and their inhabitants are your priority, also explore [journeys through Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru](/multi-country/bolivia_colombia_ecuador_peru/). We help align the country sequence, altitude tolerance, the island excursion alternative and the time between flights.

## Frequently asked questions about wildlife in the four countries

### Will we see animals in all four countries?

No. The program concentrates wildlife watching in Bolivia and the Galápagos. Peru and Colombia focus mainly on cultural sites and scenery. Sightings of individual species depend on natural conditions on the day.

### Can I visit both North Seymour and South Plaza on one itinerary?

The current tour includes one branch confirmed after booking: North Seymour with Bachas **or** South Plaza with Cape Carrión. Visiting both is not promised.

### Do I need special athletic training?

This is not a trekking expedition, but it does include high-altitude road days and walks. Assess your ability to cope with altitude and extended transfers beforehand; on the islands, follow your guides' instructions and nature-conservation rules.

buttonLabel: "Explore the journey through Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Uruguay"
lead: >-
  Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Uruguay all feature on our 32-day journey through eight South American countries. Travelers visit Uruguay for a day from Buenos Aires, then cross Chile to Bolivia's lagoons and Uyuni, continue through Peru and Ecuador with the Galápagos, and finish in Colombia. We explain how to prepare for these very different stages without mistaking the four selected countries for a standalone tour.
---

## Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Uruguay: what connects this itinerary?

You can select these four countries in the [multi-country travel](/multi-country/) filter, but the existing itinerary that includes them covers **eight countries and 32 days**. This makes a major difference when calculating flights, budgets and vacation time. The full route begins in Brazil and Argentina, with a one-day visit to Uruguay, then continues through Chile, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia. The complete day-by-day sequence appears on the ["8 South American Countries in 32 Days" tour page](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/).

Each of the four selected countries has a distinct role. [Uruguay](/uruguay/) offers a city day in Montevideo across the Río de la Plata. [Bolivia](/bolivia/) is the highest and most physically demanding segment, with lagoons, off-road vehicles and Uyuni Salt Flat. [Ecuador](/ecuador/) combines Quito with the Galápagos Islands. [Colombia](/colombia/) concludes the journey with three very different cities: Medellín, Cartagena and Bogotá.

Four checkmarks in the selector therefore mean that all four countries feature **on one actual tour**, not four consecutive border crossings. A trip restricted to this quartet would need a separate itinerary.

## Why Uruguay is a day trip and Bolivia a distinct expedition stage

Travelers reach [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) from Buenos Aires by ferry, tour the city with an English-speaking guide and return to Argentina that evening. Their main hotel remains in Buenos Aires; no additional overnight stay in Uruguay is planned. It is a compact introduction to the capital that nevertheless involves two international border procedures: entry to Uruguay and re-entry to Argentina.

Bolivia is structured in the opposite way. After [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) in Chile, a two-day off-road journey begins through high-altitude lagoons. The itinerary names Laguna Verde, the Sol de Mañana area, Laguna Colorada, a chain of other lakes and [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The next stage leads to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) and [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/), after which the group crosses into Peru.

The key concerns here are less about distances on a map than altitude, long mountain-road transfers, abrupt temperature changes and physical well-being. The tour explicitly mentions altitude sickness risk and an acclimatization stop in San Pedro de Atacama. Anyone for whom high-altitude travel may be medically unsuitable should discuss the pace before booking the entire journey, not after arriving.

## Ecuador: Quito, the Galápagos and special access requirements

After Peru, travelers fly from Lima to [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/). The city program includes the equator area and the Intiñan Museum, followed by a flight to the Galápagos. On [the Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), travelers visit Baltra and Santa Cruz, the island highlands and Puerto Ayora.

The sea excursion day has **two alternatives**, confirmed at booking: North Seymour with Bachas Beaches, or South Plaza with Cape Carrión. Both trips are not included together in the promised itinerary. This matters particularly to visitors drawn by specific animals or islands: match the desired excursion against the confirmed alternative, weather and current conservation rules.

The Galápagos have their own visitor controls. In addition to ordinary entry arrangements for Ecuador, travelers need a transit control card (TCT); check the relevant documents and procedures before flying to the islands. After the island segment, the itinerary returns to the mainland at Guayaquil and continues by air to Colombia.

## Colombia after the Galápagos: three different city experiences

The Colombian leg begins in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), with an excursion to El Peñón rock and Guatapé, followed by the city and Comuna 13. Next comes [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/), with its Caribbean coast and historic city. The journey ends in [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), combining the old center, Monserrate and an excursion to the Salt Cathedral at Zipaquirá.

Unlike high-altitude Bolivia and island-based Ecuador, Colombia requires several flights between cities, different sightseeing arrangements and a change in altitude from the coast to Bogotá. After the busy Uyuni and Galápagos programs, these transitions are especially noticeable: when changing the route privately, preserve time for rest and flight connections.

## Documents, payments and packing for the four countries

**Visas and entry.** Requirements depend on nationality and passport type. Colombia's and Uruguay's official lists allow short visa-free visits for Russian passport holders, but this does not remove immigration checks, onward-ticket requirements and other documentation. Bolivia, Ecuador and the countries also visited—Argentina, Chile and Peru—must be checked separately before departure. Pay particular attention to re-entering Argentina after the ferry and the overland crossing from Bolivia to Peru. We help prepare a checklist for the complete route and passengers' passports; entry permission can only be granted by the relevant country.

**Money.** Uruguay uses the Uruguayan peso, Bolivia the boliviano and Colombia the Colombian peso, while Ecuador's official currency is the US dollar. These present four different situations for paying small expenses, so carrying a sum of US-dollar cash does not automatically solve every payment problem. Before departure, check whether your particular cards work, fees, exchange facilities and backup payment methods in each country. This is especially important in remote highlands and on the islands.

**Clothing and health.** Pack season-appropriate light clothing for Montevideo and coastal Cartagena, warm layers and protection from wind and sun for Bolivia's lagoons, and comfortable shoes and sun protection for the Galápagos. Assess insurance against the entire itinerary, including altitude, remote locations and optional activities; standard city-break cover may differ from the protection needed in Bolivia.

## Evaluating duration and cost

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}; a meaningful comparison must use **the complete** itinerary rather than adding the four selected countries together as if they were a separate product.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

Our tour includes accommodation in four-star hotels, domestic flights, transfers and scheduled excursions. International airfare, optional excursions, unspecified lunches and other personal expenses cost extra. Individual days also have particular conditions: one of two Galápagos sea routes is confirmed, and the Uruguay visit does not add another overnight stay.

If mountain scenery is your main interest, compare the itinerary with [Bolivia tours](/bolivia/tour/); for island wildlife, explore [Ecuador journeys](/ecuador/tour/). These catalogs can help you select different geography, but do not imply that all four countries automatically appear in every program.

## Frequently asked questions about Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Uruguay

### Can I visit only these four countries on the featured tour?

No. The 32-day program also includes Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru. A shorter four-country journey must be designed separately, with flights and transfers calculated afresh.

### How long do travelers spend in Uruguay?

The itinerary provides a one-day trip from Buenos Aires to Montevideo, returning by ferry in the evening. There is no scheduled overnight stay in Uruguay.

### What is the hardest part of the Bolivian stage?

Altitude and long off-road drives through the lagoons and Uyuni. Medical limitations, acclimatization and tolerance for mountain roads should be assessed before travel.

### Are all Galápagos island excursions included?

No. One sea excursion day follows one of two alternative routes. The selected branch is confirmed after booking; both are not promised together.

### Can I pay in US dollars in all four countries?

Do not count on it. Ecuador uses USD, while the other three have national currencies. Card acceptance, currency exchange and cash requirements must be checked separately for each stage.

## Adventures in four countries: what is really included?

This selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The featured [32-day tour through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) contains Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Uruguay as **four stages of a longer journey**, not a standalone itinerary restricted to them. Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru are also visited between these stages.

The four countries differ substantially in terms of activity. In Bolivia, travelers encounter high-altitude dirt roads and jeep transfers; in Colombia, viewpoints over the Guatapé reservoir; in Ecuador, walks through volcanic island terrain. Uruguay includes a ferry journey and an introduction to Montevideo. The program does not list multi-day trekking or rafting in these four countries.

## Bolivia: 4×4 vehicles, salt flats and altitude

The two-day off-road stage begins after an overnight stay at San Pedro de Atacama in Chile. On the Bolivian side, the route crosses Laguna Verde, the Salvador Dalí Desert, Sol de Mañana geysers and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). The jeeps then continue to [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), Colchani and Incahuasi Island.

This is **a high-altitude road adventure**, not a mountain climb. Its principal features are long road sections, wind, temperature fluctuations and limited comfort in remote areas. The itinerary allows for acclimatization before Bolivia, but each traveler's tolerance of altitude must be assessed in advance. The next stage leads through La Paz and Tiwanaku into Peru.

## Colombia: El Peñón rock and city itineraries

Much later, after the Galápagos, the route reaches [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). A trip to [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) reveals the islands of the reservoir and the surrounding green hills. [The El Peñol and Guatapé excursion](/colombia/medellin/el-penol-guatape-from-medellin/) includes climbing steps to a viewpoint: the standalone excursion description specifies approximately 740 steps. This is a considerable physical effort to take into account when choosing activities.

The rest of the Colombian itinerary is largely urban: [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/), historic [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) and [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) with its surroundings. Do not expect every day in Colombia to involve hiking or extreme sports.

## Ecuador: lava tunnels and a day at sea

In Ecuador, the first excursions are in Quito before travelers fly to [the Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). On the highlands of Santa Cruz, [a walk to see giant tortoises and lava tunnels](/ecuador/santa-cruz-highlands/santa-cruz-highlands-lava-tunnels/) is planned. The volcanic origin of the islands is directly visible in the lava cavities and terrain.

The next day depends on the confirmed itinerary option: **[North Seymour with Bachas Beaches](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/north-seymour-island-tour/) or [South Plaza with Cape Carrión](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/south-plaza-island-tour/)**. These are boat trips with walks, not mandatory diving or strenuous ascents. Keep the island visits as alternatives in the itinerary, because both options are not promised together.

## Why Uruguay appears in the adventure selection

The Uruguay day comes much earlier: the group crosses by ferry from Buenos Aires to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), visits the center and returns to Argentina by ferry. [The one-day Montevideo excursion](/uruguay/montevideo/montevideo-day-trip-from-buenos-aires/) provides the experience of another country, views across the Río de la Plata and a walk through [the Old City](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/). This stage does not include sporting adventures, independent treks or an overnight stay in Uruguay.

It helps put the journey as a whole into perspective: active days on the Altiplano and Galápagos alternate with city tours, sightseeing and flights. When comparing [multi-country adventure tours](/multi-country/interests/adventure/), look beyond the number of countries to **how many days are devoted to each specific activity**.

## Frequently asked questions about the active journey

### Do I need to bring my own off-road driving equipment?

The program describes an organized 4×4 jeep route without requiring participants to drive themselves. Discuss personal belongings and equipment according to altitude and island-walking conditions.

### Does climbing El Peñón count as trekking?

It is a staircase climb to a viewing platform during an excursion, not a multi-day mountain trek. Assess your fitness before attempting the climb.

### Can I visit both Galápagos island itineraries?

The tour includes one of two alternatives. The exact branch is confirmed after booking, so both cannot be counted as part of the purchased program.

lead: >-
  Across four countries, the itinerary connects the pre-Inca city of Tiwanaku, Quito's historic districts, colonial Cartagena and old Montevideo. Uruguay is visited on a single day from Buenos Aires, while Bolivia, Ecuador and Colombia are stages of a longer journey through eight South American countries. ## Four countries, four perspectives on South American history

This catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: [a 32-day journey through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). The Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Uruguay combination filters an existing itinerary by its main countries. Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru are also visited, and the order of stops is determined by the full program.

For travelers interested in culture and history, the distinctions among historical sites are especially important. [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) tells the story of an Andean civilization before the Incas; Quito introduces a colonial city and the history of equator research; [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) reveals the defensive architecture of the Caribbean coast; and [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) explores Uruguay's urban history.

## Uruguay: Montevideo in one day, without an overnight stay

The group travels to Uruguay by ferry **from Buenos Aires**. After arriving in port, there is [a sightseeing excursion through Montevideo](/uruguay/montevideo/montevideo-day-trip-from-buenos-aires/), some free time and a return to Argentina that same evening.

The route centers on Independence Square, the port, [the Old City](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/) and the cathedral. Independence Square is home to the mausoleum of José Gervasio Artigas and the Palacio Salvo. Historic buildings, squares and views over the Río de la Plata help explain how the country's capital developed.

This day should be regarded as **a brief introduction to urban history**, not an in-depth exploration of all Uruguay. Ferry crossings take up part of the day, so sightseeing time in Montevideo is limited.

## Bolivia: Tiwanaku after Uyuni Salt Flat

After crossing Bolivia's high-altitude terrain via [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), the journey continues toward [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/). The next historical stop is [Tiwanaku archaeological complex](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/), associated with the pre-Inca culture of the Altiplano, long before the rise of the Inca state.

The program includes the ancient center's principal monuments, including the Gate of the Sun and Kalasasaya. This stage is part of [the excursion via Tiwanaku to Desaguadero](/bolivia/la-paz/tiwanaku-desaguadero-from-la-paz/), followed by an overland border crossing into Peru and onward travel to Titicaca. Tiwanaku is therefore logically visited **between La Paz and Puno**, not on an arbitrary side trip from the other end of the country.

Sun protection and clothing suitable for the highlands are useful when visiting the ancient monuments. The earlier Bolivian itinerary gives travelers time to acclimatize, but the archaeological complex still lies at considerable altitude.

## Ecuador: Quito and the equator

The group flies from Lima to Quito. The Ecuadorian capital's itinerary includes a city visit and the [Mitad del Mundo complex](/ecuador/place/mitad-del-mundo/) with [the Intiñan Museum](/ecuador/place/intinan-museum/). Quito itself is notable for the architecture of its historic center, churches and its setting amid the Andes.

Here it is useful to distinguish **the capital's historic architecture** from visitor attractions explaining the equator. Their meanings are different: one concerns urban development, the other geography and the history of measurement. After Quito, the tour flies to [the Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/), where nature and wildlife, not urban museums, become the main theme.

## Colombia: from Medellín to Cartagena's walls

In [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), the itinerary introduces [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/) and contemporary urban culture. An excursion to Guatapé adds the story of old El Peñol and the reservoir.

The next stop is [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). [The historic-center and San Felipe Castle excursion](/colombia/cartagena/cartagena-city-san-felipe-castle-tour/) includes colonial streets, city walls and fortifications. In [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), the journey continues with monuments in the capital and a visit to [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) and its Salt Cathedral. The Colombian days thus combine colonial heritage with contemporary urban life.

## Choosing historical experiences on the longer route

The order matters: Uruguay is visited from Argentina in late October; the group reaches Tiwanaku in Bolivia after Chile; Quito follows Peru; and Colombia concludes the journey. Changing the order of countries would affect both logistics and time at the historical sites.

To compare other programs, visit [all multi-country culture and history journeys](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/) or [all tours through Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Uruguay](/multi-country/bolivia_colombia_ecuador_uruguay/). Before choosing, decide what matters most: ancient Andean cities, colonial architecture or contemporary urban culture.

## Frequently asked questions about the cultural itinerary

### Is one day enough for Montevideo?

Yes, for the central sights included in the program. A single ferry day is too short for museums and a detailed independent exploration of Uruguay.

### Where are the pre-Inca monuments on this route?

In Bolivia, at the Tiwanaku stop before crossing into Peru. The visit is included in a longer transfer and requires no return journey from another country.

### Are the Galápagos part of Ecuador's cultural program?

The islands are included in the journey, but their main excursions focus on protected nature areas and wildlife. The Ecuadorian section's cultural highlights are concentrated in Quito.

## Nature in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Uruguay: what is actually included?

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring the four named countries and the "Nature" interest. The actual program is ["8 South American Countries in 32 Days"](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru are also part of it. This filter does not promise a separate product visiting only Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador and Uruguay.

Nature excursions are not distributed equally: Bolivia offers lagoons and salt flats, Ecuador the Galápagos, and Colombia the rock and reservoir at Guatapé. Uruguay includes **only a city day in Montevideo**. This is the essential difference between a thematic catalog and a journey featuring nature activities in every single country. [The general combination of these countries](/multi-country/bolivia_colombia_ecuador_uruguay/) shows tours regardless of theme.

## Uruguay: a day in Montevideo

On this tour, travelers take a ferry from Buenos Aires to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), explore the city with an English-speaking guide and return to Argentina that evening. No overnight stay in Uruguay or excursion to its nature reserves is specified.

Uruguay's beaches, dunes and marine wildlife watching could form part of other itineraries, but they are not included in this particular program. Travelers for whom Uruguay's natural landscapes are essential will need to select another product or modify the route.

## Bolivia: two days among volcanoes and salt

After Chile, the program enters high-altitude Bolivia for two organized jeep days with an English-speaking guide. The first includes [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), Polques hot springs, [Sol de Mañana](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/) and [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/). The second crosses other lagoons and the Chiguana Salt Flat to [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and a cactus-covered island.

This is a substantial nature section, but it involves considerable altitude: part of the route runs **above 4,000 meters**. An expedition-style overnight stay, dusty roads and thin air require preparation. The tour's conditions specifically mention altitude sickness risk despite the acclimatization stop in Chile. A mirror-like salt-flat surface depends on water levels and is not guaranteed.

## Ecuador: volcanic islands and a choice of sea route

Via Peru, the journey reaches Quito and then [the Galápagos](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). On [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/), travelers visit the island highlands and lava tunnels. The next day's sea excursion goes **either to [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) and [Bachas](/ecuador/place/bachas-beaches/), or to [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) and Cape Carrión**. One option is confirmed after booking.

The Galápagos are particularly interesting for their island nature and wildlife, but actual sightings depend on the excursion chosen and the weather. It would be misleading to present the highlights of both alternative branches as mandatory stops in one itinerary.

## Colombia: the rock at Guatapé and neighboring shores

After returning to the mainland via Guayaquil, travelers fly to Medellín. An eight-hour excursion goes to [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/). The rock and intricate shoreline of the reservoir create a lush green landscape unlike high-altitude salt flats or volcanic ocean islands.

Other Colombian days focus on cities, museums and the sights of Bogotá and Cartagena. No separate multi-day nature expedition is included. For that format, explore [nature itineraries in Colombia](/interests/nature/tours/colombia/).

## Choosing based on the nature program

| Country | Program |
|---|---|
| Uruguay | Montevideo |
| Bolivia | Lagoons, jeeps and Uyuni |
| Ecuador | Galápagos |
| Colombia | El Peñón and Guatapé |

This is a 32-day journey with other countries between the selected stages. It combines domestic flights (included in the tour), bus and road transfers, and cultural excursions. International airfare is paid for separately. Bolivia requires particular attention to altitude, while Ecuador calls for confirmation of the island sea-excursion alternative. ## Frequently asked questions

### Does the program include nature excursions in Uruguay?

No. It includes a sightseeing trip to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) and a return to Buenos Aires.

### Can the Bolivian stage be difficult without trekking?

Yes. The expedition travels by jeep, but some stops are above 4,000 m. Altitude and the length of the transfers matter.

### Will every Galápagos island be included?

No. The sea excursion follows one of two alternatives selected after booking.

### Where does the tour include natural scenery in Colombia?

The main confirmed nature outing goes to [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and the reservoir near [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/).
